{{Short description|Superenergy tensor of gravitational field flux-energy in a vacuum}}
In [[general relativity]] and [[differential geometry]], the '''Bel–Robinson tensor''' is a tensor defined in the [[abstract index notation]] by:
:<math>T_{abcd}=C_{aecf}C_{b} {}^{e} {}_{d} {}^{f} + \frac{1}{4}\epsilon_{ae}{}^{hi} \epsilon_{b}{}^{ej}{}_{k} C_{hicf} C_{j}{}^{k}{}_{d}{}^{f}</math>

Alternatively,
:<math>T_{abcd} = C_{aecf}C_{b} {}^{e} {}_{d} {}^{f} - \frac{3}{2} g_{a[b} C_{jk]cf} C^{jk}{}_{d}{}^{f}</math>
where <math>C_{abcd}</math> is the [[Weyl tensor]].  It was introduced by Lluís Bel in 1959.<ref>{{citation|first1=L.|last1=Bel|title=Introduction d'un tenseur du quatrième ordre|journal=Comptes rendus hebdomadaires des séances de l'Académie des sciences|volume=248|pages=1297-3000|year=1959|url=http://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/bpt6k32002/f1321.image.langEN}}</ref><ref>{{citation|first1=J. M. M.|last1=Senovilla|title=Editor's Note: Radiation States and the Problem of Energy in General Relativity by Louis Bel|journal=General Relativity and Gravitation|volume=32|page=2043|year=2000|issue=10|doi=10.1023/A:1001906821162|bibcode=2000GReGr..32.2043S|s2cid=116937193}}</ref> The Bel–[[Ivor Robinson (physicist)|Robinson]] tensor is constructed from the Weyl tensor in a manner analogous to the way the [[electromagnetic stress–energy tensor]] is built from the [[electromagnetic tensor]]. Like the electromagnetic stress–energy tensor, the Bel–Robinson tensor is totally symmetric and traceless:
:<math>\begin{align}
       T_{abcd} &= T_{(abcd)} \\
  T^{a}{}_{acd} &= 0
\end{align}</math>

In general relativity, there is no unique definition of the local energy of the gravitational field. The Bel–Robinson tensor is a possible definition for local energy,<ref>{{citation|first1=J.|last1=Garecki|first2=M.|last2=Goląb|title=The superenergy tensor of the Einstein-Rosen gravitational wave|journal=Acta Physica Polonica B|volume=11|issue=4|pages=255-257|year=1980|url=https://inspirehep.net/literature/157941}}</ref> since it can be shown that whenever the [[Ricci tensor]] vanishes (i.e. in vacuum), the Bel–Robinson tensor is divergence-free:
:<math>\nabla^{a} T_{abcd} = 0</math>
